records.real_world_identity_notes: The 1998 Toyota GT-One, chassis code TS020, was Toyota Team Europe's GT1 entrant at the 1998 24 Hours of Le Mans. Do not merge it with the revised 1999 LMGTP specification or with the single homologation road car; those versions changed the cockpit and/or hardware. The simulator identity is an exact match to this 1998 race-car family, but a particular chassis or livery is not established.
records.confidence_basis: The official 24 Hours of Le Mans history identifies the TS020 as a 1998 and 1999 Le Mans car and describes the 1998 entries as GT-One race cars. The period-specific technical review distinguishes the 1998 manual-lever cockpit from the 1999 paddle-shift revision and lists the 1998 car's six-speed Xtrac sequential gearbox.

records.specification_basis: Both sources identify a six-speed sequential gearbox for the GT-One. The sources call it an Xtrac six-speed sequential gearbox with hydraulic shift assistance. They do not establish a dog-ring or synchromesh construction, so the broader sequential category is used. The 1998 specification is explicitly described as having a manual shift lever only in the cockpit; the paddle system belongs to the 1999 revision/test conversion. A sequential gearbox operated by the 1998 manual lever establishes one-gear-at-a-time sequential selection. No source reviewed establishes a first-gear gate position. The full-resolution photograph shows a conventional rim with a flattened lower section, so the project's rim taxonomy classifies it as d-shaped rather than gt-formula. The full-resolution photograph shows no display on the rim. The technical review separately identifies a wheel display as an addition for LM802's later paddle-shift test conversion, not the original 1998 race wheel. The full-resolution photograph visibly shows the upper section of the conventional D-shaped rim removed/open. The full-resolution photograph shows no shift-light elements on the rim. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip.
